justification: Closes the DATA half of DQ-30 with a production database write: 241 rows in regulatory_provisions held zone codes that do not exist in their LGA, 112 of them live and served on the compliance surface. Adds a write-time guard in the applicability tagger so those codes cannot be stored again, plus the repair script. Production data mutation on the table behind the property-assessment provisions panel — critical by any reading.

pre_impl.existing_data: regulatory_provisions.v2_applicable_zones (text[]) across ~55,634 rows carrying zone codes; lep_zone_coverage (26 LGAs, is_complete=TRUE) as ground truth; lga_registry for slug-to-LGA resolution. No schema change of any kind.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: If an LGA has no complete lep_zone_coverage rows, nothing is filtered and nothing is repaired — those rows are reported UNVERIFIABLE rather than assumed valid or assumed invalid. Absence of ground truth is never treated as a pass, which is the exact failure that let DQ-30 be marked fixed while it was still broken.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Applies to every existing row holding an invalid code, not only newly tagged ones, because re-deriving from provision text was measured against production first and repaired 0 of 241 — it re-runs the identical regex that produced them.
pre_impl.external_source_error: Both scripts read only the Postgres database; there is no external API in this path. On any exception the backfill rolls back its open transaction and re-raises rather than committing a partial repair.
pre_impl.frontend_type: No frontend type change. v2_applicable_zones remains a string array end-to-end; only the member values change, and 'ALL' was already an established sentinel in that column.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: If the repair were wrong a user would silently see a DCP provision that does not apply to their property, or lose one that does. Mitigated by taking a backup first, verifying its row count before any UPDATE, guarding each row on its pre-change value, and confirming the result with a check that can fail.

functions.name: main
functions.input: Command-line arguments; dry-run unless --apply is passed. Reads candidate rows and the ground-truth zone lists from the database.
functions.output: A printed repair plan grouped by council and, under --apply, per-row guarded UPDATE statements against regulatory_provisions plus a backup table.
functions.if_none: When no row needs repair it reports that every resolvable row is already valid and exits zero without opening a write transaction at all.

functions.name: _resolver
functions.input: An open cursor and the ground-truth mapping, used to build a council-slug to ground-truth-key resolver mirroring the validator exactly.
functions.output: A closure returning the matching ground-truth key for a council slug, or None when that council cannot be resolved to any complete coverage.
functions.if_none: Returns None, and the caller skips that row entirely rather than guessing a mapping — an unresolvable council is never repaired blind.

functions.name: load_slug_resolution
functions.input: An open cursor plus the ground-truth zone mapping, reading active rows from lga_registry to translate council slugs.
functions.output: A dictionary mapping every registry slug to its ground-truth key, or to None where no case-insensitive match exists in the coverage table.
functions.if_none: A slug resolving to None makes its rows UNRESOLVED, reported as its own defect rather than folded into unverifiable and quietly ignored.

values.value: lep_zone_coverage zone codes per LGA where is_complete is true
values.if_missing: No filtering and no repair occur for that LGA; rows are reported UNVERIFIABLE so that missing ground truth can never read as a clean pass.
Rows with a null or empty array are excluded by the query itself, so there is nothing to repair and nothing is written for them.

values.value: lga_registry slug, display_name and parent_lga for active councils
values.if_missing: The council resolves to None and its rows become UNRESOLVED, surfacing a registry naming defect instead of silently skipping a quarter of the corpus.

queries.purpose: Select candidate provision rows holding zone codes for possible repair
queries.where_clause: WHERE v2_applicable_zones IS NOT NULL AND cardinality(v2_applicable_zones) > 0 AND source_council IS NOT NULL. Deliberately not filtered by is_current: this repairs stored data rather than serving it, and excluding superseded rows would knowingly leave 129 of them holding codes that do not exist.

queries.purpose: Guarded per-row repair of one provision's zone array
queries.where_clause: WHERE id = %s AND v2_applicable_zones = %s — optimistic concurrency on the exact pre-change value, so a row altered by another writer is skipped and counted rather than clobbered.

queries.purpose: Load the per-LGA ground-truth zone list used by both validation and repair
queries.where_clause: WHERE is_complete = TRUE AND lga IS NOT NULL AND zone IS NOT NULL

break_it.scenario: The query that loads the per-LGA ground-truth zone list returns a stale or incomplete set, so the repair drops a zone code that is genuinely correct and hides a provision from properties it really governs.
break_it.what_happens: A user in the affected zone stops seeing a DCP control that applies to their land, which is exactly the class of silent omission DQ-30 was opened to fix.
break_it.how: Filtering only runs where is_complete is true, pre-change values are preserved in regulatory_provisions_zone_backup_20260801, and the script prints a single-statement rollback. Coverage itself was gate-verified per project-zone-permissibility-unblocked-2026-07.
break_it.repro: UPDATE regulatory_provisions t SET v2_applicable_zones = b.v2_applicable_zones FROM regulatory_provisions_zone_backup_20260801 b WHERE t.id = b.id; then re-run the validator.

break_it.scenario: A row whose every stored code is invalid becomes ALL, so a provision that was previously invisible now appears against every property in that council area.
break_it.what_happens: Twenty live rows widen from matching no property to matching all of them, adding noise to the provisions panel for those councils.
break_it.how: Measured before applying rather than discovered afterwards: 92 live rows narrow, 20 widen, 129 are not served. ALL is the pre-existing sentinel for undetermined applicability, and showing a possibly-irrelevant control is a smaller harm than hiding a binding one.
break_it.repro: SELECT id, source_council FROM regulatory_provisions WHERE v2_applicable_zones = ARRAY['ALL'] AND id IN (SELECT id FROM regulatory_provisions_zone_backup_20260801);

break_it.scenario: Someone later calls the tagger without valid_zones in the bulk pipeline, so the write-time guard silently does nothing and invalid codes accumulate again.
break_it.what_happens: The database drifts back toward the pre-repair state one extraction at a time, with no error raised anywhere.
break_it.how: validate_zone_code_validity.py exits non-zero on any invalid row so it can be run as a gate and fails loudly rather than degrading quietly. The parameter defaults to None specifically to keep the function pure for the golden tests, which is why the standing check matters.
break_it.repro: python scripts/validate_zone_code_validity.py — exit code 1 with a per-council breakdown of offending rows.

break_it.scenario: The backup table already exists from an earlier partial run, so CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS keeps stale contents and the recorded rollback state does not match what is about to be overwritten.
break_it.what_happens: A rollback would restore values from the wrong point in time, quietly reintroducing whatever was stored during that earlier run.
break_it.how: The backup row count is read back and compared against the size of the repair plan before any UPDATE runs, and the script aborts with a non-zero exit when the backup is smaller than the plan.
break_it.repro: Create the backup table with fewer rows than the plan, then run with --apply and confirm it aborts before writing.

break_it.scenario: A council slug fails to resolve to ground truth, so its rows are skipped by the repair and quietly stay invalid while the run reports success.
break_it.what_happens: Invalid codes survive in a council nobody realises was skipped, and the summary gives false assurance that the repair was complete.
break_it.how: Resolution handles all three verified join hazards: parent_lga holding a slug rather than a display name, case differences such as Ku-ring-gai against Ku-Ring-Gai, and City of Sydney against Sydney. Anything still unresolved is reported by the validator as its own UNRESOLVED category, never as a pass.
break_it.repro: python scripts/validate_zone_code_validity.py and read the UNRESOLVED line and the slug list printed beneath it.

post_merge.db_reset: Already executed against production: 241 rows repaired, 0 skipped, pre-change values retained in regulatory_provisions_zone_backup_20260801 with a one-statement rollback printed by the script.
post_merge.secrets: No new secrets or environment variables; both scripts use the existing DATABASE_URL already required across the repository.
post_merge.other_repo: No other repository or service requires a corresponding change; every consumer of this column lives in this repository.
post_merge.manual_verify: Load a Woollahra or Ku-ring-gai address on the assessment page and confirm the provisions panel still renders sensibly, since 20 live rows widened from matching no property to matching all properties in their council.
